t.E235.agn: In 2009 EFSA stated that the data were not robust enough to set its own ADI (JECFA's ADI is 0.3 mg/kg body weight). It concluded that the proposed levels do not raise a safety concern when used only for the surface treatment of semi-hard and semi-soft cheese rinds and certain sausage casings, and that there is no concern regarding antimicrobial resistance.
t.E235.body: Natamycin is hardly absorbed from the intestine at all: it could not be detected in the blood of people who took 500 mg. In rats, almost all of it is excreted in the faeces; in the large intestine it is broken down by bacteria into inactive fragments.
t.E235.found.0: Rind of hard and semi-hard cheeses
t.E235.found.1: Outer surface of dried sausages and salamis
t.E235.prod: Produced by fermentation with Streptomyces natalensis.
t.E235.regx.0: EFSA could not set an ADI (JECFA ADI 0.3 mg/kg); no safety concern for surface use on cheese rinds and sausage casings only, and no concern regarding antimicrobial resistance.
t.E235.summary: An antifungal produced by bacteria through fermentation. It prevents mould on cheese rinds and the surface of dried sausages.
t.E235.what: It inhibits the growth of mould and yeast on the surface of cheese rinds and sausage casings.
